verdictBasis: The decision merits pass completely and both claimed repairs landed and verify. The single SHOULD-FIX is that the subject's own title still says 'turn 2' while it is the turn-3 subject, contradicting its Protocol line four lines below. This is the fourth instance of turn-metadata drift in this family and the same class I have graded SHOULD-FIX three times, each accepted and repaired by the coordinator.

shouldFixRecorded.location: line 1 — '# D-067 turn 2 — File 08 MF-6 notes for preview owner recordings', read against line 5
shouldFixRecorded.finding: The subject's title identifies it as turn 2 while it is the frozen subject of a turn-3 review, and it contradicts itself inside its own header block: line 5 reads '> **Protocol:** D-000 new cycle, turn 3 of 3.' The disposition table three lines further down records the turn-2 findings ADV-D067-T2-01 and ADV-D067-T2-02 as ACCEPTED, so the document simultaneously claims to be turn 2 and records turn 2 as concluded.
shouldFixRecorded.provenance: I traced the title across all three drafts rather than assuming. The turn-1 draft reads '# D-067 —' with no turn marker, which was correct. The turn-2 edit deliberately introduced the marker, giving '# D-067 turn 2 —', which was correct then. The turn-3 edit advanced line 5 to 'turn 3 of 3' and left line 1 untouched — a byte-identical title between the turn-2 and turn-3 drafts. So this is a defect introduced by the turn-3 revision, not one I let pass earlier.
shouldFixRecorded.whyThisGrade: Consistency. I have graded exactly this class three times in this family — the 'not yet dispatched' status on D-051/052/053 turn 1 and on D-067 turn 1, and the stale 'turn 1 of 3' on D-051/052/053 turn 2 — and the coordinator accepted and repaired all three. It is also the defect that sent D-059 to CONTESTED, where I graded a subject's turn self-misidentification a NOTE, the other reviewer graded it higher, and I recorded a self-correction accepting that the harder grading was right. Grading a stale turn marker a NOTE here would abandon a standard the coordinator has already acted on three times.
shouldFixRecorded.whyNotMustFix: It touches no decision content, and the draft title does not survive adoption — adopted entries render as '## D-0NN — <title>' with no turn marker, as D-061, D-066 and D-068 all show — so the stale marker never reaches the register.
shouldFixRecorded.fix: One word: '# D-067 turn 3 — File 08 MF-6 notes for preview owner recordings.'

priorFindingsDisposition.status: REPAIRED, verified, and the repair is better than the fix I proposed
priorFindingsDisposition.verification: 'disposed count' now appears zero times and 'qualifying set' once: clause 2 reads "Condition 1's qualifying set is a separate union: (a) rows whose leading label is `SATISFIED`, plus (b) rows whose status cell carries an exact scoped owner-recording note." It then adds a sentence I had not thought to ask for — 'The two components are counted separately in the snapshot: one SATISFIED and six explicitly disposed, with set-union deduplication if a future row has both' — which resolves the collision and also handles the case of a row that later satisfies both limbs.

selfCorrection: ADV-D067-T2-02 is the same defect I recorded at turn 2 as NOTE-C2-D067-T2-01, graded one level higher by the other reviewer, and the repair confirms the higher grade was right. What makes this worth recording rather than shrugging at is that I wrote the decisive argument into my own note — 'the preamble's whole purpose is to instruct regeneration', and a regenerator applying clause 2's definition would have written 7 where the snapshot said 6 — and then graded it a NOTE anyway on the ground that no number in the entry was wrong. A definition that is immediately used with a different extension is a defect in the definition, and 'the arithmetic is stated explicitly elsewhere' is a reason the error is survivable, not a reason it is not an error. Separately, ADV-D067-T2-01 I missed outright: at turn 1 I confirmed the snapshot heading existed and at turn 2 I confirmed the quoted regeneration sentence was verbatim, but I never asked whether the heading's own date would go stale once the snapshot's contents changed underneath it. That is the same pattern as the DR-G08 miss on product-boundary-preview.v1 — checking that a cited thing resolves without checking what it will resolve to after the act being authorized. This is also why I am not softening today's finding: having under-graded turn metadata once in this engagement and once before at D-059, doing it a third time to avoid a contested outcome would be the error, not the remedy.
summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only, and both predecessors remain frozen, so the full three-turn lineage is auditable. Both claimed repairs landed and verify: the snapshot heading advance quotes file 08 verbatim, and the terminology collision I recorded as a note at turn 2 is resolved with a better fix than I proposed. A full diff bounds the turn-3 edit to the Protocol line, two disposition rows, the qualifying-set rewrite, the new heading clause and the resulting renumbering — clause numbering runs 1 through 7 with no internal cross-references left dangling, and the six-row notes table, alternatives and readiness sections compare byte-identical to turn 2. All four measured inputs still match live bytes and file 08 remains unedited. My objection is one word: the title says turn 2.

objectNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX, and I want the shape recorded precisely, because this is turn 3 and the consequence is a contested outcome rather than another revision. The decision merits pass and have passed since turn 2. Both repairs claimed this turn landed and verify, one of them fixing a defect I under-graded as a note. Nothing about the file-08 edit this entry authorizes is in question. The objection is that the subject's title says turn 2 while its Protocol line says turn 3 of 3, four lines apart, above a table recording turn 2 as concluded. I considered whether being at turn 3 should move me to a note, and rejected that: D-000 clause 2 says in terms that a forced consensus is never recorded as consensus, so softening a grade to avoid CONTESTED is the one thing the protocol forbids me to do here. I have graded this class three times in this family and the coordinator accepted and repaired it every time; the fix is one word.
